issues.failure_explanation: gimel_1 is the H^1(Omega)-seminorm of the elliptic-projection error of u_0. For a degree-p_x Lagrange space the H^1 error of any approximant decays at most like h^{p_x}, so the correct bound is h^{2 min(p_x, s-1/2)} p_x^{-(2s-1)} ||u_0||^2_{s+1/2}; the stated h^{2 min(p_x+1, s-1/2)} is the L^2-type rate and is false for s-1/2 > p_x (e.g. u_0 smooth, non-polynomial). The same paper uses the correct H^1 exponent min(p_x,s) for gimel_8.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace min(p_x+1, s-1/2) by min(p_x, s-1/2) in (estimate-gimel1) and in the statement of Theorem h-p-convergence.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed a priori estimate in Theorem h-p-convergence over-states the spatial rate of the u_0 term by one power of h; the corollary rates (tau^p with h=O(tau)) are unaffected.
issues.title: Wrong spatial exponent in the bound on the initial-datum term gimel_1 (H^1-seminorm error of the elliptic projection)
issues.why_classification: A local correction of one exponent; all conclusions, rates in the corollary, and scope survive.

issues.failure_explanation: The corollary uses a single Sobolev index s and, for s <= p, claims the rate tau^{s-1/2}. With alpha=1, h=O(tau), p_x=p_n^t=p and s <= p, Theorem h-p-convergence bounds gimel_5 by tau^{min(s-1,p+1)} = tau^{s-1} (the norm involves Delta u^{(s-1)} only) and gimel_6 by h^{min(p+1,s-1)} = h^{s-1} (u'' in L^2(H^{s-1}) only). Both are strictly worse than tau^{s-1/2}. The proof only discusses gimel_3 and gimel_7 and asserts the remaining terms are fine, which is only true in the smooth regime s >= p+2. Hence the second estimate of the corollary is not established under its stated hypotheses.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either weaken the conclusion to tau^{s-1} under the uniform-s hypotheses, or add the extra regularity hypotheses needed for gimel_5 and gimel_6 (Delta u in H^{s-1/2}(L^2) on each I_n and u'' in L^2(H^{s-1/2})), and state them explicitly in the corollary.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised 'optimal in terms of the Sobolev scaling' estimate for solutions of finite regularity s <= p is unsupported as stated; the numerical confirmation claim for test case 2 rests on it.
issues.title: Singular-regime rate tau^{s-1/2} in the corollary is not implied by Theorem h-p-convergence (gimel_5 and gimel_6 only give tau^{s-1})
issues.why_classification: The result survives after adding explicit (natural) regularity hypotheses on Delta u and u''; no new argument is needed, only a corrected hypothesis/exponent bookkeeping.

issues.failure_explanation: Trefethen's Theorem 7.2 requires nu >= 1 and bounds ||f - f_n||_infty by 2V/(pi nu (n-nu)^nu) where V is the total variation of f^{(nu)}; it never yields a bound in terms of ||f'||_infty alone (that would be the excluded case nu = 0, where uniform convergence can even fail). Thus (infty-1) with c_3(p)=1/(p-2), i.e. inf_q ||v-q||_infty <= (2/(pi(p-2)))||v'||_infty on [-1,1], is not a consequence of the cited result. Moreover, by the classical sharp asymptotics for the class {|f'|<=1} on [-1,1] (sup E_p ~ pi/(2p), Favard constant K_1=pi/2), the constant 2/(pi(p-2)) ~ 0.64/p is too small for large p, so the stated inequality is false for suitable scalar (hence Bochner) v.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (infty-1) by a Jackson-type inequality with a valid explicit constant (e.g. inf_q ||v-q||_infty <= (pi/(2(p+1)))(tau_n/2)||v'||_infty, i.e. c_3(p)=pi^2/(4(p+1))) and propagate the new constant through eta_{2,n}, osc_n(f) and the reliability estimates.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit constants c_3(p_n^t-1), c_3(p_n^t-3) entering eta_{2,n}, osc_n(f) and the 'constant free' reliability bound are unjustified and, for larger p, too small; the qualitative structure and p-scaling of the estimator survive but the claimed guaranteed upper bound does not.
issues.title: Explicit constant c_3(p)=1/(p-2) in the L^infty best-approximation estimate is not supported by the cited Trefethen theorem and contradicts sharp Jackson/Favard asymptotics
issues.why_classification: A standard replacement inequality with an explicit constant of the same p^{-1} order restores every claim; only numerical constants in the estimator change.

issues.failure_explanation: (i) The paper asserts that Delta u in L^2(L^2) implies Delta u_tau in L^2(L^2); this does not follow from the regularity of u. It can be shown (via R u_tau'' - Pi^0 Delta u_tau = Pi^0 f and an induction over the slabs using continuity of u_tau) only from Delta u_0 in L^2, an argument the paper does not give. (ii) The proof and the estimator use Delta(R u_tau - u_tau) in L^2 and the norms ||[Delta u_tau'](t_{n-1})||_{L^2}. On I_1, R u_tau - u_tau = [u_tau'](0) phi(t) with [u_tau'](0) = u_tau'(0^+) - u_1, so Delta(R u_tau - u_tau) in L^2 and finiteness of eta_{2,1} require Delta u_1 in L^2, i.e. u_1 in H^2(Omega); assumption (assumption:convexity) only gives u_1 in H^1_0. Under the stated hypotheses the identity (initial-identity-for-error-equation) is not an L^2 identity and the right-hand side of the reliability bounds is +infinity (vacuous). Proposition reliability-estimate states no data hypothesis at all.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add u_1 in H^2(Omega) cap H^1_0(Omega) to (assumption:convexity), state the assumption in Proposition reliability-estimate, and supply the short inductive argument showing Delta u_tau (and Delta R u_tau) in L^2(L^2).
issues.overall_effect: The reliability estimates are vacuous unless u_1 in H^2 cap H^1_0; the claimed sufficiency of (assumption:convexity) for the a posteriori analysis is not established.
issues.title: A posteriori analysis needs Delta u_tau, Delta R u_tau in L^2: the implication from Delta u in L^2 is unproved and the jump term at t_0 requires u_1 in H^2, not assumed
issues.why_classification: A standard extra data hypothesis plus a short local argument restore all claims with unchanged estimator, constants and rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We construct a computable error estimator
Given~$m$ as in~\eqref{choice-xi}, for all $ n=1, \dots,m-1$,
Find the interval index $m$ where $\eta_1$ attains the maximum and set $\xi = t_{m-1}$.

issues.failure_explanation: eta_2 = sum_{n=1}^m eta_{2,n}, osc(f), and (for p_n^t=2) c_4(p_n^t-3) all depend on m, defined in (choice-xi) as the slab containing the maximizer xi of ||u - R u_tau||, which involves the unknown exact solution u. Hence eta as defined cannot be evaluated from u_tau alone, contradicting the stated computability and the 'constant free reliable' guarantee as a practical bound. The numerically used surrogate (m=N, xi=t_N) is not an upper bound for the true estimator: the m-th slab term in the proven bound has weight 2 tau_m (no c_3/pi factor), whereas with m=N that slab receives the smaller weight (2/pi) tau c_3(p-1) < 2 tau (and for p>=3, tau^3 c_2 c_3(p-3)/pi < tau^3 c_2), so eta^{(N)} may underestimate eta^{(m_true)}. The adaptive ESTIMATE step's choice of m via eta_1 is likewise unjustified (eta_1 concerns u_tau - R u_tau, not u - R u_tau).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine the estimator as the maximum over m=1,...,N of the m-dependent bounds (eta_2^{(m)} + osc^{(m)}(f)), which is computable and still reliable with the same constants, or bound every slab with the weaker uniform weights; then redo the numerical efficiency/adaptivity tests with the reliable estimator.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition reliability-estimate is true only for the non-computable m; the estimator actually implemented in Sections on efficiency and adaptivity has no proven reliability, undermining the 'computable, constant free, reliable' contract and the adaptive algorithm's ESTIMATE step.
issues.title: The error estimator eta is not computable: eta_2, osc(f) and c_4 depend on the index m determined by the unknown exact solution; the version used numerically (m=N) is not proven reliable
issues.why_classification: A contained redefinition of the estimator (max over m) restores a reliable, computable bound with comparable p- and tau-scaling, but the estimator as defined and as tested must be replaced and the numerical evidence re-established.
